name: Singapore Management University
description: Singapore Management University is a publicly funded university established in 2000, with a city campus in Singapore's Bras Basah district. It specialises in business, economics, accountancy, law, computing and the social sciences, taught in a seminar-style format.
whyIncluded: One of Singapore's MOE-funded Autonomous Universities, and the local reference point for business, economics and law degrees that Singaporean students often compare with overseas alternatives.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Business Management
programmes.notes: Annual tuition for AY2026/27 entering freshmen from SMU's official 'Tuition Fees & Grant' page, fixed for the normal 4-year candidature (one rate for all non-Law degrees). Citizen S$11,550 (Tier A Tuition Grant) and PR S$16,100 (Tier B), both excl. GST (GST subsidised by the Government). International S$26,200 = Tier C Tuition Grant rate for non-ASEAN students, incl. 9% GST (ASEAN S$25,150; non-subsidised S$47,700). Compulsory fees = 2026 annual miscellaneous student fees: S$281 (SC/PR) or S$367 (international), charged each Term 1. admissions.smu.edu.sg blocks bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-09-30, hence sourceType secondary. The page shows only the AY2026/27 cohort; no earlier years' figures are published there.

programmes.name: Master of Science in Financial Economics (MSFE)
programmes.notes: Self-funded programme. Official MSFE page: tuition fee S$54,500 inclusive of GST for the whole programme, divided by the 18-month full-time duration (flexible to 12 months). The page shows the fee next to the January 2027 and August 2027 application windows without naming the intake; feeYear 2026 covers the January 2027 (AY2026/27) intake. No Citizen/PR tier: SMU publishes no subsidised or SC/PR rate for this programme. masters.smu.edu.sg blocks bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-09-30, hence sourceType secondary.

programmes.name: Juris Doctor (JD)
programmes.notes: Self-funded graduate-entry law degree (no MOE Tuition Grant). Official Yong Pung How School of Law page 'Finance & Administrative Matters for JD Programme, Admit Year 2026': tuition fee for the entire programme S$81,750 incl. GST, the same for all nationalities, billed in four instalments over the first two years (S$5,000 advance deposit + S$15,437.50 + 3 x S$20,437.50); divided here by the 3-year full-time candidature. One-off fee = non-refundable registration fee on offer acceptance: S$400 for Singaporeans/PRs, S$500 for international students. Textbooks and course materials are extra. law.smu.edu.sg blocks bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-09-30, hence sourceType secondary. Only the 2026 admit year is published.

programmes.name: Master of Laws (LLM)
programmes.notes: Self-funded programme (no MOE subsidy). Official SMU LLM 'Fees & Scholarships' page: tuition fee for the August 2027 intake S$39,240 incl. GST for the whole one-year programme (Judicial Studies, Cross-Border Business and Finance Law in Asia, and Law and Technology tracks), the same for all nationalities; the page says the 2027 figure is indicative and subject to revision. It includes a non-refundable S$8,000 tuition deposit, which is not counted separately. Compulsory fees = annual miscellaneous fees from the 2027 intake: S$400 (Singaporeans/PRs) or S$480 (foreigners), excl. GST. Application fee S$100 excluded. The Dual LLM (Singapore & London) track costs S$37,605 to SMU plus GBP 22,975 to QMUL. law.smu.edu.sg blocks bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-09-30, hence sourceType secondary. No earlier intake's fee is published on the page.
